children: Oppenheimer is pointing investors toward two lesser-known stocks with substantial upside potential as Wall Street enters the final quarter of 2026, even as elevated oil prices, geopolitical tensions and higher interest rates complicate the market outlook. The investment bank's analysts see gains of as much as 66% over the next 12 months in FuelCell Energy
and Innoviva
, citing opportunities in AI infrastructure and specialty healthcare.
Oppenheimer chief investment strategist John Stoltzfus remains constructive on equities, arguing that positive fundamentals have repeatedly helped markets recover from bouts of volatility.
He believes markets are adjusting to a new normal rather than heading toward a period of sustained downside risk.
The first pick, FuelCell Energy, develops modular fuel-cell systems capable of supplying scalable, on-site electricity to commercial and industrial customers.
Five-star analyst Colin Rusch assigned FCEL an Outperform rating and
$24 price target
, implying approximately 42% upside from $16.90.
Rusch believes the company's power-generation technology positions it to capitalize on growing data-center electricity demand.

FuelCell announced an agreement with Fit Energy in June involving up to 380 megawatts of on-site power capacity. Its fiscal third-quarter backlog increased 4% to $1.3 billion, although revenue declined 29% to $33 million.
Rusch sees the potential for FuelCell to eventually generate $1.5 billion in revenue and more than $300 million in EBITDA as production scales.
Oppenheimer's second pick, Innoviva, combines a respiratory drug royalty business with a growing portfolio of critical-care and infectious-disease treatments.
Analyst Les Sulewski rates INVA Outperform with a
$35 price target
, suggesting 66% upside from $21.11.

His thesis centers on the market potentially undervaluing Innoviva's specialty therapeutics business, which delivered 26% year-over-year growth in U.S. product sales to $36.6 million during the second quarter.
Investors Takeaway
For FuelCell, converting its sizeable backlog into actual revenue while narrowing losses will be crucial to supporting Rusch's bullish projections.
Innoviva investors should monitor specialty therapeutics sales growth, new product commercialization and whether respiratory royalties can continue financing expansion.
Importantly, both Oppenheimer targets reflect potential returns over the coming 12 months, rather than guaranteed gains before the end of 2026.

title: Oppenheimer Sees Massive Upside in 2 Stocks
